---
title: "Puzzle #19 — Count Printed Page Digits"
description: "A mathematical explanation of an Algorithmic Puzzles problem, from small cases to proof."
---

## 1. State the problem clearly

The page labels of a book are 1,2,3,...,N, and printing all those labels uses exactly **1,578 decimal digits**. How many pages are there? The trap is to divide 1,578 by a guessed average length.

## 2. Start with the simplest useful observation

Count the groups whose digit lengths are easy: pages 1–9 use one digit, 10–99 use two, and 100–999 use three.

## 3. Express the relationship mathematically

$$
D(N)=9+2(90)+3(N-99)\quad(100\le N\le999)
$$

**Explain every symbol:** D(N) is the number of printed decimal digits for pages 1 through N. The 9 counts one-digit pages; 90 counts pages 10–99; the factor 2 gives two characters for each of them; N−99 counts three-digit pages from 100 to N.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Substitute D(N)=1,578: first 9+2×90=189 characters cover pages 1–99. Remaining 1,578−189=1,389 characters belong to three-digit page labels. Divide by 3: 1,389/3=463 further pages. So N=99+463=**562**.

## 4. Derive the answer and prove it works

The piecewise approach is exact because no page in the range 100–999 uses a different number of digits. As a check: pages 100–562 number 463, using 1,389 digits, and the first 99 use 189. Their sum is 1,578.

## 5. Check the result step by step

This is an example of partitioning a count by **place value**, not counting each page separately. For a much larger book, add the four-digit group 1,000–9,999 with 4 digits per page, and so on.

## 6. What survives when the numbers change?

How many digits are required to print pages 1–120? Work through the same three groups.

## 7. Try it yourself

Counting, place-value ranges, piecewise arithmetic.

**Techniques:** undefined.

**Book reference:** Levitin and Levitin, *Algorithmic Puzzles* (Oxford University Press, 2011), Easier #19, printed p. 36; hint p. 73; solution p. 94.. The explanation and formulation here are written independently.
